name: HGH (Somatropin)

b.x: The Rudman study changed how the world thinks about aging. In 1990, a six-month trial gave recombinant growth hormone to men over 60 and tracked an 8.8% increase in lean body mass with a 14.4% decrease in adipose tissue (NEJM) [1]. That single paper launched three decades of research into somatropin. Somatropin (brand names Genotropin, Humatrope, Norditropin, Omnitrope) is a 191-amino-acid protein produced via recombinant DNA technology. It's identical to endogenous human growth hormone. Unlike secretagogues that stimulate your pituitary to release GH, somatropin is the hormone itself. Subcutaneous bioavailability runs about 70 to 80 percent on the US labels that state it. Serum levels peak about 3 to 6 hours after the injection. US labels put the subcutaneous half-life at about 2 to 4 hours, including 2.0 hours for Norditropin in healthy adults. Norditropin also gives an apparent 7 to 10 hours in GHD patients. The biological effects, mediated through IGF-1, persist 20 to 24 hours. The FDA has approved somatropin brands for pediatric GHD, adult GHD, Turner syndrome, Prader-Willi syndrome, and HIV-associated wasting. Current labels add small-for-gestational-age and idiopathic short stature, SHOX deficiency and Noonan syndrome; each brand carries its own subset. Nutropin AQ, the brand for growth failure in chronic kidney disease, is no longer licensed. Off-label use centers on anti-aging (1 to 2 IU daily), body recomposition (2 to 4 IU), and athletic performance (4 to 6 IU). Sleep quality improvement is the first thing users notice, often within the first two weeks. The KIMS database, tracking 15,809 GH-treated adults, confirmed neutral effects on lipids and glucose at appropriate doses and found no increased malignant cancer incidence [2]. A 2007 meta-analysis of randomized trials in healthy older adults found 2.1 kg more lean mass and 2.1 kg less fat [4]. Bone density didn't change. In a 6-month trial of 52 older men, knee and grip strength didn't improve [5]. Insulin resistance remains the side effect that demands the most monitoring.

Somatropin binds to the growth hormone receptor (GHR), a transmembrane receptor that sits as a preformed dimer on cell surfaces. Binding triggers a conformational change that activates Janus Kinase 2 (JAK2), a tyrosine kinase physically linked to the receptor's intracellular domain. JAK2 phosphorylates tyrosine residues on the GHR itself, creating docking sites for STAT proteins. STAT5b is the primary downstream signal. Once recruited and phosphorylated by JAK2, STAT5b dimerizes and translocates to the nucleus. There it drives transcription of target genes. The most important product is IGF-1 (insulin-like growth factor 1), produced mainly by the liver; IGF-1 mediates most of somatropin's anabolic effects. Protein synthesis accelerates. Cell proliferation increases. Apoptosis slows. Two additional pathways matter. The MAPK/ERK pathway promotes cell growth and differentiation. The PI3K/Akt pathway regulates glucose metabolism and cell survival, which partly explains why somatropin antagonizes insulin signaling at higher doses. Somatropin's direct lipolytic action operates through a separate mechanism that doesn't involve IGF-1 at all. Hormone-sensitive lipase activation in adipocytes breaks down stored triglycerides. This is why fat loss, particularly visceral fat, is one of the most consistent and dose-dependent effects. The dual mechanism (IGF-1-mediated anabolism plus direct lipolysis) is what makes somatropin effective for body recomposition.
HGH (Somatropin) benefits center on body composition, recovery, and measurable improvements in quality-of-life markers backed by clinical trial data.
Rudman's 1990 trial [1] showed 8.8% lean body mass increase and 14.4% fat mass decrease in 12 men over 60 after six months of GH three times a week.
The KIMS database followed 15,809 GH-deficient adults for a mean 5.3 years. Lipids and fasting glucose stayed neutral, and new cancers ran in line with the general population [2].
Sleep quality improvement is the most consistently reported early benefit across community forums; users describe deeper sleep and vivid dreams within the first one to two weeks.
Skin elasticity and thickness improve measurably between months three and six. Nails and hair grow noticeably faster. These collagen-mediated effects track with rising IGF-1 levels.
Bone mineral density gains require patience. Meaningful DEXA changes typically don't appear before 12 months of consistent therapy.

Workout recovery and injury healing speed are among the top reasons athletes and bodybuilders use somatropin, though a 6-month randomized trial in 52 older men found no gain in knee or grip strength [5].
Partially Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 15 key studies · FDA-approved
Strong evidence for body composition improvements (lean mass, fat loss) and bone density in GH-deficient adults.

Dosing studied: 0.15–0.3 mg/day (0.45–0.9 IU/day) start for adult GHD per the Norditropin label, raised 0.1–0.2 mg every 1–2 months; 1–4 IU/day in clinical anti-aging studies; max ~4 IU/day in most adult GHD protocols

Moderate evidence for general anti-aging and wellness use in healthy older adults: a 6-month RCT in 52 men over 69 showed +4.3% lean mass / -13.1% fat mass (Papadakis 1996) [5]. Long-term safety in non-GHD populations remains unresolved. That trial found no significant gain in knee or grip strength.
Key Study

Rudman et al. NEJM 1990 (PMID 2355952): foundational 6-month controlled trial (12 treated men, 9 untreated); KIMS database 15,809 patients long-term safety (PMID 35368070); Liu 2007 meta-analysis (PMID 17227934): +2.1 kg lean mass, -2.1 kg fat in healthy older adults; Papadakis 1996 RCT (PMID 8633830): no strength gain at 6 months; Frontiers in Aging 2025 clinical review (PMID 40260058)
Limitations

Most RCTs ≤12 months in duration; anti-aging use in healthy adults lacks dedicated long-term RCTs; 2024 Swedish registry study (3,408 treated as children, 50,036 controls) found HR 1.28 for all neoplastic events, significant in males only; malignant tumors did not rise (HR 0.91); no 2024–2026 RCT specifically studying 1–2 IU/day in healthy aging adults
Community Experience
Widely trusted as the gold standard for body recomposition and anti-aging.
Community dosing: 1–2 IU/day (anti-aging/wellness); 2–4 IU/day (body recomposition); 4–6 IU/day (bodybuilding)

Pharma-grade is universally respected for purity; grey market quality is the primary controversy. Anti-aging community considers 1–2 IU/day a conservative, sustainable protocol; bodybuilding community uses 4–6 IU/day with AAS.
What users report (6)
Improved deep sleep quality (most consistently reported, within 1–2 weeks)
Faster recovery from training and injuries
Visceral fat reduction, especially abdominal (noticeable at 8–12 weeks)
Skin texture and elasticity improvement (3–6 months)
Accelerated nail and hair growth
Improved sense of well-being and energy
Common issues (6)
Cost: #1 reason for discontinuation; pharma-grade is prohibitively expensive for long-term off-label use
Water retention (hands, feet): first 4–6 weeks, usually resolves with dose reduction
Carpal tunnel / hand tingling: most common side effect requiring dose reduction
Morning fasting blood glucose elevation
Grey market quality inconsistency: underdosing and counterfeit risk widely reported
Lean muscle gains at anti-aging doses (1–2 IU) are modest and slow: often described as overhyped

Science and community agree on body composition benefits (lean mass gain, fat loss). Diverge on: (1) dose thresholds: community anti-aging doses (1–2 IU) sit above the Norditropin label's adult GHD starting dose (0.45–0.9 IU) but below most trial doses; (2) indication: community uses predominantly for off-label anti-aging/performance, which FDA prohibits; (3) muscle strength: community reports improved performance but a 6-month RCT in older men found no significant strength gain (PMID 8633830).

Community Community use: 1-2 IU/day for anti-aging, 2-4 IU/day for body recomposition, 4-6 IU/day for bodybuilding. The Norditropin label starts adults with growth hormone deficiency at about 0.2 mg (0.6 IU) a day. [Source](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/021148s062lbl.pdf)

Somatropin is dosed in IU, not mcg. One IU equals roughly 0.33 mg. That conversion trips people up initially. If you're using lyophilized powder (not a ready-to-use pen), mix it with the diluent that comes with your product. Brands differ: Omnitrope's 5.8 mg vial ships with bacteriostatic water (benzyl alcohol), Zomacton 10 mg with bacteriostatic water (metacresol) and Zomacton 5 mg with bacteriostatic saline (FDA labels). For a 10 IU vial with 1 mL of diluent, each 10 units on an insulin syringe equals 1 IU. A 1 IU daily dose means drawing to the 10-unit mark. At 2 IU, draw to 20 units. At 0.5 IU for the ramp-in phase, that's 5 units on the syringe. Pens skip this math entirely. Norditropin FlexPro comes ready-mixed, and a Genotropin cartridge is mixed inside its own pen. Dial the dose and inject. Inject on an empty stomach. Carbohydrates blunt GH action. Morning fasted or pre-bed are the two most common timing windows. Splitting the dose (AM plus pre-bed) becomes relevant above 3 IU daily. Store reconstituted vials at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius and never freeze them. US labels set room-temperature limits brand by brand. A Norditropin pen in use keeps 3 weeks at up to 25 degrees Celsius; mixed vials of the other brands stay refrigerated. IGF-1 labs every three months. That's the number that tells you whether your dose is working and whether it's too high.
Cycling Protocol

For anti-aging doses (1-2 IU), many practitioners run continuously with periodic IGF-1 monitoring rather than cycling. At higher doses (4+ IU), 6 months on / 1 month off helps maintain insulin sensitivity. Some protocols use 5 days on, 2 days off weekly to reduce cost and manage sides.
HGH (Somatropin) Cycle

Exogenous HGH suppresses endogenous pituitary GH secretion via IGF-1 negative feedback and somatostatin upregulation. Extended continuous use can reduce pituitary GH response capacity: though the clinical significance varies by dose and duration. At therapeutic doses (1–2 IU/day), many practitioners run continuously with periodic IGF-1 monitoring rather than strict cycling. At higher doses (4+ IU/day), 6 months on / 4–8 weeks off is standard practice to allow IGF-1 normalization, insulin sensitivity recovery, and pituitary axis reassessment. The 5 days on / 2 days off weekly schedule is a popular cost-reduction strategy with community reports of similar efficacy.
IGF-1 above 400 ng/mL (supraphysiological): time for break or dose reduction
Fasting glucose consistently above 100 mg/dL: insulin resistance accumulation
HbA1c trending upward over consecutive quarters
Carpal tunnel or edema not resolving with dose adjustment
Set out your vial, the diluent supplied with it (brands differ, so check the label), alcohol swabs, and a 29 to 31 gauge insulin syringe (0.5 mL or 1 mL).

If using a lyophilized vial for the first time, reconstitute by drawing the diluent volume your product's label gives into the syringe (the math below uses 1 mL). Inject slowly along the vial wall. Never shake the vial; swirl gently until the powder dissolves completely.

With a 10 IU vial reconstituted in 1 mL of diluent, each 10 units on a 100-unit insulin syringe equals 1 IU. For a 30 IU vial in 1 mL, each 3.3 units equals 1 IU; for a 36 IU vial in 1 mL, each 2.8 units equals 1 IU.

b.h: Swab the vial top with alcohol
b.x: Draw the appropriate number of units. Remove air bubbles by tapping and slowly pushing the plunger until a tiny drop appears at the needle tip.
Choose an injection site: abdomen (2 inches from the navel), outer thigh, or upper arm. Clean the site with an alcohol swab.
Pinch a fold of skin and insert the needle at a 45 to 90 degree angle. Inject slowly. Hold for 5 seconds before withdrawing.
Rotate injection sites with each dose to prevent lipodystrophy.

Timing: inject fasted (30 to 60 minutes before food) in the morning for fat loss protocols. Pre-bed injection mimics natural circadian GH release and is preferred for sleep-focused or FDA-labeled GHD protocols. Above 3 IU daily, split into AM fasted plus pre-bed.
Store reconstituted vial in the refrigerator at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Use within 14 to 28 days depending on brand. Never freeze.
Alternative Routes
Subcutaneous (SC)
Reference standard; ~70–80% bioavailability on US labels. Inject into abdomen, thigh, or upper arm.

Rotate sites to prevent lipodystrophy. Peak serum GH at about 3–6 hours. Insulin syringes (29–31G) are standard. Norditropin FlexPro pens hold a ready-mixed solution; Genotropin cartridges are mixed inside the pen before first use.
Intramuscular (IM)
Peak at about 3 hours vs 4–6 hours SC, with higher total exposure (AUC 194 vs 134 ng·h/mL) in 12 healthy volunteers (PMID 1490668). No US label gives an IM dose.
Used clinically in some pediatric protocols. More painful for daily injections. No evidence of superior efficacy over SC for adult use. SC is universally preferred for self-administration.
Intravenous (IV)
Immediate but very short-lived peak; pharmacokinetically inferior for therapeutic use
IV route is used only for GH stimulation testing (GHRH + arginine test) under clinical supervision. Not appropriate for therapeutic or off-label protocols.
Works With
IGF-1 LR3
HGH drives endogenous IGF-1 production; exogenous IGF-1 LR3 adds direct anabolic signaling. Advanced body recomposition/hypertrophy stack. High-risk combination.
40–80 mcg IGF-1 LR3 SC, 5 days on/2 days off, post-workout
Tesamorelin

GHRH analog approved for HIV-associated lipodystrophy; sometimes stacked with low-dose HGH at clinics for visceral fat reduction. May be redundant when running full HGH: occasionally substituted on off-weeks for cost savings.
2 mg/day SC tesamorelin on HGH off-days
Sermorelin
Cost-saving substitute for HGH on weekends (5 on/2 off strategy). Stimulates endogenous GH release on off-days to maintain GH pulse continuity.
200–300 mcg SC pre-bed on HGH off-days
CJC-1295 / Ipamorelin
Stacked on HGH off-days or weeks to sustain GH axis stimulation at lower cost. Do NOT run high-dose secretagogues simultaneously with high-dose HGH: creates supraphysiological GH levels.
CJC-1295 no-DAC 100–200 mcg + Ipamorelin 100–200 mcg SC, pre-bed, on HGH off-days only
Avoid
Oral estrogen (estradiol, conjugated estrogens)

Oral estrogen significantly reduces hepatic IGF-1 production in response to GH: women on oral HRT or oral contraceptives may require 2–3x higher HGH doses to achieve equivalent IGF-1 response. Transdermal estrogen has substantially less impact. Not dangerous but severely reduces efficacy.
Glucocorticoids (prednisone, hydrocortisone, dexamethasone)

Glucocorticoids attenuate GH growth-promoting effects and impair IGF-1 signaling. HGH may reduce 11β-HSD1 activity, altering cortisol conversion; in adrenal insufficiency patients on replacement therapy, HGH can unmask adrenocortical insufficiency requiring glucocorticoid dose adjustment. Monitor carefully.
Somatostatin analogs (octreotide, lanreotide, pasireotide)
Somatostatin analogs suppress GH secretion, so they blunt any GH secretagogue. They are used to block GH in acromegaly and work against HGH too (community stack guidance).
Insulin (concurrent high-dose stack)

The HGH + insulin "bodybuilding stack" creates severe hypoglycemia risk. HGH raises blood glucose (insulin resistance); exogenous insulin lowers it. Miscalculation can be fatal. Requires continuous glucose monitoring. Community labels this as advanced-only with experience and CGM.
Brand Price

Norditropin FlexPro (Novo Nordisk): ~$750 (5 mg pen) to $7,040 (15 mg pen pack) US retail, no insurance. Genotropin (Pfizer): ~$7,667 retail / ~$2,244 discounted cash price. At 1 IU/day: ~$576–$960/month at clinic rates; at 2 IU/day: ~$1,152–$1,920/month.
Compounded
No compounded price is listed. FDA says licensed biologics such as somatropin are not eligible for the 503A and 503B compounding exemptions (March 2020 notice).
Pricing updated 2026-04-09

Insulin resistance is the side effect that requires the most attention. Somatropin directly antagonizes insulin's action on glucose uptake. At doses above 2 IU daily, fasting blood glucose begins trending upward in many users. This can unmask pre-diabetes or worsen existing glycemic control. HbA1c should be checked every three to six months. Fasting glucose above 126 mg/dL is a clear signal to reduce the dose or pause the protocol. Peripheral edema is the most common complaint by volume. Swelling in the hands and feet (peripheral edema) hit 42% of GH-deficient adults in Norditropin's 6-month trial, vs 8% on placebo. It's fluid retention, not inflammation. The body adjusts within a few weeks for most people. If pitting edema develops or swelling involves the face and neck, other causes should be investigated. Carpal tunnel syndrome showed up in 2% of 3,031 GH-deficient adults in Genotropin's extension studies. In anti-aging trials of healthy older adults, a 2025 review puts it at 7 to 50% [3]. Fluid retention compresses the median nerve, producing wrist tingling and hand numbness. This is the most frequent reason for dose reduction in community reports. Reducing by 0.5 IU daily and holding for two to four weeks typically resolves it. Almost always reversible. Joint pain and muscle stiffness affect roughly 20% of users, concentrated in the first few weeks. Both track with dose; both tend to settle as the body acclimates. A 2025 review puts breast tenderness or gynecomastia at 7 to 14% in two trials of older men [3]. At doses above 4 IU daily for extended periods, some users report jaw growth and increased shoe size. These are signs of acromegaly-like effects from prolonged supraphysiological IGF-1 levels. Cancer risk generates the most anxiety. The KIMS database (15,809 patients) found no increased malignant cancer incidence at therapeutic doses. A 2024 Swedish registry study followed 3,408 people treated as children against 50,036 matched controls for a median 19.8 years [6]. Neoplastic events overall ran higher (HR 1.28), significant in males only. Malignant tumors didn't rise (HR 0.91). Active malignancy remains a strict contraindication because GH and IGF-1 can promote tumor growth in existing cancers. Injection site reactions (redness, mild pain) are standard for subcutaneous administration. Rotating sites prevents lipodystrophy over long-term use. GH can unmask central hypothyroidism by increasing T4-to-T3 conversion. Monitor TSH and free T4, especially if IGF-1 levels aren't responding as expected. Hypothyroidism itself blunts the IGF-1 response. When to seek medical attention: persistent carpal tunnel after dose reduction, fasting glucose consistently above 110 mg/dL, visible changes in facial bone structure or extremity growth, or unexplained rapid weight gain with edema. Intracranial hypertension is a label warning that's easy to miss. Headache, vision changes, nausea or vomiting can signal it, usually within the first 8 weeks. Labels call for an eye exam before starting and periodically after, and stopping if papilledema shows up. US label contraindications: active malignancy, active proliferative or severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy, and acute critical illness after major surgery, trauma or respiratory failure. Also listed: children with Prader-Willi syndrome who are severely obese, have a history of upper airway obstruction or sleep apnea, or have severe respiratory impairment. Hypersensitivity to somatropin or its excipients is on the list, as is growth use in children whose epiphyses have closed. A past cancer isn't on that list, but labels require it to be inactive and fully treated first. Pregnancy isn't either; labels say the human data are too limited to judge the risk.
Common Issues & Solutions
Carpal tunnel / wrist tingling: First sign of excess dose. Reduce by 0.5 IU/day and hold for 2–4 weeks before increasing again. Usually fully reversible. Does not require stopping protocol.
Persistent water retention beyond week 6: Consider reducing dose or switching to 5 on/2 off protocol. Avoid high-sodium foods. If edema is pitting or involves face/neck, evaluate for other causes.

Fasting glucose elevated (90–110 mg/dL range): Standard at therapeutic doses. Time injection pre-bed rather than morning to reduce postprandial impact. Add resistance training. Consider metformin if consistently above 100 mg/dL fasting.

IGF-1 not responding (stays below 150 ng/mL at 2 IU/day): Consider product quality issue, especially with grey market kits. Hypothyroidism can blunt IGF-1 response: check TSH. Oral estrogen in women significantly reduces hepatic IGF-1 output.

No noticeable effects at 8+ weeks: Verify product quality via third-party peptide testing service or serum GH test 3–4 hours post-injection. Ensure injection is truly subcutaneous (not intradermal), rotate sites, check storage against the product label (mixed vials at 2–8°C, never frozen).

Oral estrogens: reduce IGF-1 response to GH; women on oral estrogen may need higher GH doses

Pharma-grade (Norditropin, Genotropin, Omnitrope) is prescription-only but not a federally controlled substance, and prohibitively expensive off-label ($1,000–$2,000+/month). Grey market Chinese kits (Ansomone, Jintropin, Hygetropin) dominate off-label use but carry significant quality risks: community widely reports underdosing (10 IU Chinese kits reportedly act like 5–6 IU pharma), lot-to-lot variability, counterfeit risk, and potential harmful fillers. FDA says licensed biologics such as somatropin are not eligible for the 503A and 503B compounding exemptions.

b.x: Source: US labels, section 12.3: SC half-life 2.0 h (Norditropin, healthy adults), 2.3 h (Zomacton), 2.5-2.8 h (Omnitrope), 3.0 h (Genotropin, GHD adults), 3.8 h (Humatrope); Norditropin also gives an apparent 7-10 h in GHD patients

Somatropin is FDA-approved. Lilly's Humatrope is the oldest licensed somatropin brand; Drugs@FDA and the Purple Book date its first approval to October 16, 1986. Current approved brands include Norditropin (Novo Nordisk), Genotropin (Pfizer), Humatrope (Lilly), Zomacton (Ferring), Serostim (EMD Serono) and Omnitrope (Sandoz). Omnitrope is often called a biosimilar, but FDA's biosimilar list includes no somatropin product. It is not a federally controlled substance; 21 CFR 1308 lists no somatropin, and Schedule III there covers anabolic steroids, substances related to testosterone. The Anabolic Steroids Control Act of 1990 instead rewrote 21 U.S.C. 333(e) to cover HGH. A prescription is required for all legal use. Approved indications include pediatric and adult GHD, Turner syndrome, Prader-Willi syndrome, and HIV-associated wasting (Serostim). Current labels add short stature from being born small for gestational age, idiopathic short stature, SHOX deficiency and Noonan syndrome. Nutropin AQ, the brand licensed for growth failure in chronic kidney disease, had its license voluntarily revoked, per FDA's Purple Book. Anti-aging is not an FDA-authorized use of somatropin. Federal law makes it a crime to knowingly distribute HGH for any use other than an FDA-authorized treatment on a physician's order (21 U.S.C. 333(e)). Since March 23, 2020, FDA has regulated somatropin as a licensed biological product. FDA says biological products licensed under section 351 of the PHS Act are not eligible for the 503A and 503B compounding exemptions. A product sold as compounded somatropin is not a licensed product. Somatropin is prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) at all times, both in-competition and out-of-competition (2026 Prohibited List, S2.2.3). An athlete with a medical need, such as growth hormone deficiency, can apply for a Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE). Anti-doping tests for GH began in 2004 [7]. The isoform test sees only recent doses, because injected GH clears fast. A biomarker test, accepted by WADA in 2012, was meant to reach further back. That longer window does not appear to have held up in practice [8]. Grey market (non-prescription) HGH carries legal risk and quality concerns. Distributing HGH for an unauthorized use, or holding it to distribute, carries up to 5 years in prison, a fine, or both. The cap is 10 years if someone under 18 is involved (21 U.S.C. 333(e)). This content is for educational and research purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice.

phases.name: Ramp-in
phases.syringeUnits: 5 units (10 IU vial + 1 mL diluent → 10 IU/mL)
phases.notes: Start low to assess water retention and carpal tunnel sensitivity. Inject on empty stomach: carbs blunt GH action.

phases.name: Maintenance
phases.frequency: Daily (or 5 days on / 2 days off to reduce cost)
phases.notes: Target IGF-1 200–300 ng/mL. Adjust dose based on labs, not symptoms alone. 5/2 protocol saves ~30% cost with minimal efficacy loss per community consensus.

protocols.duration: 24 weeks on, 4–8 weeks off; many practitioners run continuously at this dose with periodic IGF-1 monitoring
protocols.monitoringNotes: IGF-1 at baseline and every 3 months; fasting glucose and HbA1c every 3–6 months; TSH at baseline

phases.name: Ramp-in

phases.name: Working dose
phases.timing: Fasted morning or split AM + PM

phases.name: Initiation
phases.notes: Norditropin label (2025): start near 0.2 mg a day, range 0.15–0.3 mg. Consider a lower start and smaller steps in older adults. Oral estrogen users may need more. The label's weight-based option is not for obese patients.

phases.name: Titration to maintenance
phases.dose: 0.15 mg/day and up (0.45 IU/day and up), set by response and IGF-1
phases.syringeUnits: 4.5 units and up (10 IU vial + 1 mL diluent)
phases.notes: Raise by 0.1–0.2 mg a day every 1–2 months on response and IGF-1. Lower it on adverse reactions or IGF-1 above the age- and sex-normal range. Maintenance doses vary widely; the weight-based regimen caps at 0.016 mg/kg a day (Norditropin label).

protocols.duration: Indefinite for diagnosed GHD; reassess annually
protocols.monitoringNotes: IGF-1 every 6 months (target mid-normal for age/sex); fasting glucose and HbA1c every 6 months; thyroid panel at baseline and annually; DEXA at baseline and annually

phases.name: Base building
phases.notes: Allow body to adapt. Assess glucose response. Often run concurrent with TRT.

phases.name: Peak protocol
phases.timing: Split: 2–3 IU AM fasted + 2–3 IU post-workout or pre-bed
phases.notes: At 4+ IU/day, insulin resistance becomes clinically significant: monitor fasting glucose closely. Stacking with exogenous insulin is extremely high-risk; community warns this combination is for experienced users with full understanding of hypoglycemia risk. Consider metformin co-administration if glucose elevates.

protocols.monitoringNotes: Fasting glucose weekly; IGF-1 every 6–8 weeks (target 350–500 ng/mL range at higher doses); HbA1c every 3 months; DEXA annually; monitor for carpal tunnel, jaw growth, shoe size changes (acromegaly-like signs at very high doses)

faqs.q: What is the difference between somatropin brands?
faqs.a: The licensed somatropin brands (Norditropin, Genotropin, Humatrope, Omnitrope, Zomacton, Serostim) contain the same 191-amino-acid recombinant hGH. Saizen's license was voluntarily revoked, per FDA's Purple Book. Differences are delivery device, formulation (liquid vs lyophilized), and cost. Omnitrope (Sandoz) is often called a biosimilar, but FDA's biosimilar list includes no somatropin product.

faqs.q: What is the recommended somatropin dosage for adults?
faqs.a: FDA-labeled adult GHD replacement: start at 0.15-0.3 mg daily (roughly 0.5-1 IU), titrate based on IGF-1 levels. Community anti-aging protocols run 1-2 IU daily. Performance doses range from 3-6 IU daily. Always start low; side effects scale directly with dose.

faqs.q: How much does pharmaceutical somatropin cost?
faqs.a: Brand-name Norditropin or Genotropin runs roughly $1,200-2,000 per month retail at 2 IU/day. Omnitrope runs $800-1,200/month at a discounted cash price. No compounded price is listed, since FDA says licensed biologics such as somatropin are not eligible for the 503A or 503B compounding exemptions. Insurance coverage requires documented GH deficiency.

faqs.q: What blood tests should you monitor on HGH?
faqs.a: IGF-1 is the primary marker: check at baseline, 4 weeks, and every 3 months. Target is upper-normal for age. Fasting glucose and HbA1c every 3-6 months to catch insulin resistance. Lipid panel annually. PSA for men over 40. Watch for IGF-1 exceeding the reference range, as supraphysiological levels carry long-term risk.

The FDA label supports long-term use for diagnosed GH deficiency. The KIMS database (Pfizer) followed 15,809 adults with GH deficiency for a mean 5.3 years, with a favorable safety profile (PMID 35368070). Concerns center on insulin resistance, cancer risk from sustained IGF-1 elevation, and carpal tunnel. Dose matters: replacement-level dosing (1-2 IU) carries far less risk than performance dosing (4-8 IU).
HGH (Somatropin) typically comes in 10IU or 30IU or 36IU vials. Add 1mL of the diluent its directions name to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of HGH (Somatropin)?
faqs.a: The half-life of HGH (Somatropin) is ~2-4 hours SC. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: Rudman's 1990 trial put it on the map: 8.8% more lean mass and 14.4% less body fat after six months of injections three times a week, in 12 men over 60. Somatropin (HGH) is a 191-amino-acid recombinant protein identical to the growth hormone your pituitary gland produces. It carries FDA approval for pediatric and adult growth hormone deficiency, Turner syndrome, and HIV-associated wasting.
